brief.text:
The clearest new fact this morning is a security one: Saudi Arabia's energy ministry has confirmed another strike on the East-West Pipeline, the line carrying crude from the Arabian Gulf production hubs westward, and the IMO has issued a warning about the mounting human toll of continued attacks on merchant ships in the Middle East, Red Sea and Black Sea. For anyone fixing tankers out of the Gulf, that combination matters because war-risk insurance premiums and crew-safety refusals are priced into every Arabian Gulf voyage, and because pipeline damage can shift barrels back onto ships.

On today's prices, crude is softer: Brent at 91.47 dollars a barrel, down 1.10 (-1.2%), and WTI at 85.75, also down 1.10 (-1.3%), with the Brent-WTI spread at 5.72. Products followed, gasoil down 1.2% at 4.16 dollars a gallon and gasoline down 0.8% at 2.63. The data here does not show why crude fell; I would not tie it to the pipeline headline. Bunker fuel — VLSFO, the low-sulphur fuel most ships burn — split by region today: Fujairah up 16.00 to 881.00 dollars a tonne and Singapore up 10.00 to 864.00, while Rotterdam fell 6.50 to 733.00 and Houston fell 20.50 to 750.00. That East-of-Suez premium raises voyage costs on Gulf and Asian legs. No freight index has refreshed since Monday: the Baltic Dry Index, which tracks dry bulk rates, stood at 2,854 points on Monday, up 1.7%, with the Panamax index at 2,037 (up 9.2% versus 3 November) and the Supramax index at 1,810 (down 1.4%). The tanker ETF BWET was 583.03 on Monday, down 13.8% — the data does not explain that drop.

Running stories: the Hormuz attacks thread developed today via the confirmed pipeline strike and the IMO's warning. The Black Sea strikes, shadow-fleet sanctions, chokepoint transit and Gulf congestion picture, the US West Coast port labour standoff and the Russian diesel export ban all had no fresh news in today's data and are unchanged. A separate theme worth logging is navigation interference — a webinar flags rising GPS jamming and spoofing in busy waterways.

Watch two things. First, whether tanker TCEs — time charter equivalent, the daily earnings a voyage implies — refresh after Sunday's readings, given VLCC TD3C was 1,303,616 dollars a day on 8 November. Second, thermal coal demand, which Intermodal describes as strengthening into the winter heating season, against Monday's dry indices.

storylines.title: Attacks and blockade enforcement around Hormuz
storylines.what: Attacks on commercial shipping and energy infrastructure in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued into November, including crew abandoning a tanker, a US strike on a bulker in the Gulf of Oman, and a Houthi hit on Saudi Aramco's headquarters. Saudi Arabia has now confirmed another strike on the East-West Pipeline.
storylines.why_it_matters: Hull strikes, crew abandonment and infrastructure damage raise war-risk premiums and crew-safety objections for Arabian Gulf liftings, shrinking the pool of willing owners and potentially pushing pipeline barrels back onto ships.
storylines.latest: Saudi Arabia's energy ministry confirmed another strike on the East-West Pipeline, and the IMO publicly called for stronger protection of merchant ships and crews amid continued attacks.
sources: Saudi Arabia Confirms Strike on East-West Pipeline
IMO Warns of Mounting Human Toll as Attacks on Commercial Shipping Continue

storylines.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
storylines.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, and Russia says its forces hit three cargo vessels it claims carried military goods for Ukraine, plus two electricity substations.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
storylines.latest: No Black Sea-specific news today; the IMO's warning on attacks in the Black Sea restates the risk rather than adding developments.
sources: IMO Warns of Mounting Human Toll as Attacks on Commercial Shipping Continue

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: US sanctions have expanded across Cuban maritime and energy entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks, while analysts describe the dark fleet as a parallel fleet that has tripled in size since 2022.
storylines.why_it_matters: Registry fraud, AIS spoofing and blocked-property designations force charterers, insurers and class societies to re-verify documentation and positions, pushing tonnage out of mainstream trades and tightening compliant tanker supply.

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG even as VLCC traffic declined, with Red Sea traffic up and Arabian Gulf waiting elevated. Iraq says it has reached understandings with the US to export oil through Hormuz via a lane near Oman.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts, routing lanes and waiting times determine voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.

storylines.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
storylines.what: A contract standoff involving about 250 security workers threatens operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals, while dockworkers have struck across Europe and beyond over arms shipments.
storylines.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.

storylines.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
storylines.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: US sanctions have expanded across Cuban maritime and energy entities and Iranian false-flag registry networks, while analysts describe the dark fleet as a parallel fleet that has tripled in size since 2022.
storylines.why_it_matters: Registry fraud, AIS spoofing and blocked-property designations force charterers, insurers and class societies to re-verify documentation and positions, pushing tonnage out of mainstream trades and tightening compliant tanker supply.

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG even as VLCC traffic declined, with Red Sea traffic up and Arabian Gulf waiting elevated. Iraq says it has reached understandings with the US to export oil through Hormuz via a lane near Oman.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts, routing lanes and waiting times determine voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.

storylines.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
storylines.what: A contract standoff involving about 250 security workers threatens operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals, while dockworkers have struck across Europe and beyond over arms shipments.
storylines.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.

storylines.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
storylines.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.
